newsitem.title: MACAU: Macau protesters demand school places for children.
newsitem.headline: Macau protesters demand school places for children.

text.p: Scuffles broke out in Macau between police and protestors on Friday as over a thousand people gathered outside the governor's palace demanding children living illegally in the enclave be allowed to attend schools.
More than 1,500 parents and children demonstrated outside the governor's palace of the Portuguese-administered territory in mid-afternoon, police and witnesses said.
The protestors handed government officials a petition which listed 1,173 children unable to attend schools because they were illegal immigrants or had overstayed visitors' visas.

Scuffles broke out when the demonstrators -- many carrying banners saying "We want to study" and "We want to go to school" -- refused to leave the area, blocking traffic until police forced them to move.
A police spokesman said no one was arrested, and there were no reports of injuries.

Police sources said the parents, mostly from China's Fujian province, were legal residents of Macau, but that their children had been born outside the enclave and had yet to go through proper Chinese exit permit procedures before getting residential status in the territory.
The children were believed to have entered Macau illegally or had overstayed visitors' visas, and could not be enrolled in the territory's schools, the sources said.
Most of the children involved in the demonstration were former students of an illegal study centre that the government closed down in March last year.

While the Basic Law, the constitution that takes force after Macau reverts to Chinese rule in December 1999, gives right of abode to all children of Macau residents, regardless of birth place, the government says the current law does not.
